meta.title: Render Order Test Fixture
meta.description: RENDER_ORDER_MASTER_PLAN's own fixture, created 2026-09-10. ⚠️ IT EXISTS SO THE GLASS MAP DOES NOT HAVE TO CARRY A THIRD JOB. GLASS is the physics map; adding render geometry to it split its main pane (the crack demo's lattice went 48x24 to 32x24) and its patrolling guards were already contaminating every before/after pixel diff. Director: "vamos com a 2, cria o mapa de teste de render". THE FOUR CASES, and each is here on purpose: (1) OCCLUDER CROSSING A PANE — the concrete pillar at gu (7,8), 3 storeys. This is the case GLASS does not contain and the reason this map exists. It is 2 GU NEARER than the front pane and tall, which is what makes it cross: screen_y = (x+y)*8 - level*20, so a wall 2 GU nearer (Δd=16) draws 128 px LOWER and only reaches the pane once it is about ΔL≈6.4 levels taller. A short pillar cannot do it, which is why the second one at (10,8) is 1 storey — it reaches the pane's foot and no further, so covered and uncovered are both in one capture. (2) WALL BEHIND A PANE AT THE SAME LEVELS — brick at (6..8,4). It must stay VISIBLE THROUGH the glass; losing it is finding F2, the trap that killed the first merge design. (3) TWO PANE DEPTHS ON ONE LEVEL — the back pane at (5..10,3) against the front at (4..11,6), so a level's glass needs bands rather than one split. (4) WALL IN FRONT, SAME LEVELS, NOT CROSSING — concrete at (2..3,9), the plain z bug. ⚠️ NO GUARDS, DELIBERATELY: a patrolling guard moves between two boots and shows up as noise in every pixel diff. That is not hypothetical — it is how a wrong reading got published on 2026-09-10 and had to be retracted. Keep this map still. ⚠️ agent_start is (9,9) FOR FRAMING, not for gameplay: the camera centres on the agent, and from further south the pane and the pillar sit at the top edge of the capture.
